title: I made a multiplayer fps you can play in the browser!
author: vmg-dev
selftext:
I made a multiplayer fps that you can play for free in the browser. The game mode is conquest like in battlefield. I definitely did not build this in one shot. One issue I ran into for example was levels on each side of the map being exposed with the default procedural generation so spawn camping was pretty easy. 

The environment is completely procedurally generated and there are multiple biomes. For the character and weapon models I'm using are from Quaternius. I haven't had the success other people are having generating assets, especially humanoids  
  
Play it here: [https://snack.game/u/vmg12/breachpoint](https://snack.game/u/vmg12/breachpoint)

comments.author: c0desurfer
comments.body:
Insane. Which tools did you exactly use? AI model, MCP servers and so on, what was your setup.  
Did you buy any low poly packs?  
Can you write more about your process?

replies.author: vmg-dev
replies.body:
Thanks :) 

My process is very minimal / boring. Current llms are pretty terrible at humanoid assets so I used this asset pack from Quaternius which is completely free: [https://quaternius.com/packs/toonshootergamekit.html](https://quaternius.com/packs/toonshootergamekit.html)

Everything else is procedural generation. The trick I use to get the best results is to tell the model what I want and I tell it to research it on the web. Then I have it create a tool where I can view all the different procedurally generated assets at a glance and I can tell it what's good and what isn't. 

For physics I use [jolt-ts](https://github.com/snackdotgame/jolt-ts) and [jolt-ts-character-controller](https://github.com/snackdotgame/jolt-ts-character-controller), which are typescript bindings to jolt that I open sourced.

For tools I don't really use anything other than my own platform for hosting the games (snack.game). You can install the cli which has a starter project with skills for physics / netcode. 

I also wrote a guide on multiplayer game netcode here if you want to skip all of that:

[https://snack.game/guides/real-time-multiplayer-game-networking](https://snack.game/guides/real-time-multiplayer-game-networking)

  
Full transparency: I'm the creator of [https://snack.game](https://snack.game), I have 0 way to make money from it right now

comments.author: AshinaBeats
comments.body:
wow you made me spend a good 10 minutes just shooting! good job.

The main shooting mechanics is solid, it feels good. The NPC AIs are also decently done, and that's pretty hard to get right for an indie FPS. The character models are cute, the overall aesthetic of the game feels fun and casual, with the right amount of complexity in the level design too.

I'd say the core game mechanics is there! There is a lot of ways to cheese and spawn camp right now, so I'd say you shouldn't spend much time on additional features, and focus on getting the game balance right.

Advice for your development: Make the NPC AIs better at shooting, then just let the game run for long batches at a time. Log all the actions of all AIs. Then feed all of the log files into a smart model like Opus5, and let it analyze for any bad game balances. This will help you adjust balances a lot even when you don't have enough people playing to get actual live data.

replies.author: AshinaBeats
replies.body: I just realized that you created the platform website also. The platform has potential but still needs a lot of work and need strong differentiating factors. But if I were you I would focus on getting this FPS game brushed up and getting it out there. A strong in-house flagship title is essential for any game platform, and I think this one is a perfect candidate for that.

replies.author: vmg-dev
replies.body: Ty for the feedback and ty for playing my game

comments.author: AlberionLive
comments.body: Are you just doing the server hosting yourself? Given that it's a 16 player server cap I would imagine so.

replies.author: vmg-dev
replies.body:
The site it's on does the hosting (I built it). You can build and host your own games on it for free if you want too. 

It uses web transport instead of websockets so you get udp on the browser instead of tcp.

Question about multiplayer testing. How are you testing the multiplayer version? Assuming you are lone dev.

replies.author: vmg-dev
replies.body: Multiplayer was actually the least work once I told it to use jolt-ts with deterministic physics and client side prediction with rollback.  Since it's deterministic all I need to do is sync player inputs and the rest of the simulation plays out on its own.
